results.observation: Looked for thin walls, shells, or membrane features. The part is a SOLID cylinder (plain shaft): front and right clean views show fully filled rectangular profiles with no inner outline, and the top view is a solid disc silhouette with no concentric bore ring. The iso wireframe shows only the hidden far end-face edge (dashed arc), not a shelled cavity. With no shell/hollow anywhere, the entire cross-section is bulk material, far exceeding the 0.8mm FDM minimum. No thin-wall risk exists.

results.rule_description: Overhang angle should not exceed 45 degrees from vertical without support
results.observation: Looked for overhanging surfaces, bridges, and >45-degree slopes. The part is an axisymmetric cylinder whose axis is on Z (top view is the circular cross-section; front/right are the rectangular side profiles). In its natural axis-vertical print orientation the cylindrical wall is 0 degrees from vertical (fully self-supporting) and the only horizontal face is the flat top, which is not an overhang. No unsupported overhang geometry is present. (Note: if the slicer were to lay the shaft on its side, the upper curved quadrants would exceed 45 degrees — but that is a setup/orientation choice, and the geometry is trivially self-supporting when printed on-axis.)

results.rule_description: Minimum feature size >= 0.5mm for reliable printing
results.observation: Looked for small protrusions, thin pins, embossed text, and fine detail. Across all 8 views the part is a single monolithic cylinder with no pins, ribs, text, chamfers, or micro-features. The smallest dimension present is the cylinder diameter, which is a large bulk dimension. No sub-0.5mm feature exists to be at risk.

results.rule_description: All features must have adequate clearance for manufacturing tool access
results.observation: Looked for recessed features, internal cavities, and deep/blind holes where a tool (or, for 3DP, the deposition path) could not reach. The part is a fully external convex cylinder with no bores, pockets, undercuts, or hidden internal geometry (confirmed by the wireframe views showing no internal solid edges beyond the far end-face silhouette). Every surface is openly accessible from outside; nothing is occluded.

results.rule_description: Prefer symmetric features to reduce setup operations and fixturing complexity
results.observation: Looked at overall symmetry and feature placement. A right circular cylinder is fully axisymmetric about its Z axis and mirror-symmetric across every plane through that axis, which is the maximally symmetric case. No asymmetric feature placement exists that would add setups or fixturing complexity.

results.rule_description: Horizontal holes should use a teardrop profile to prevent sagging at the top of the hole.
results.observation: Looked for circular holes oriented parallel to the build plate. The part contains NO holes of any orientation — it is a solid shaft with no bore. The rule is therefore satisfied vacuously (no horizontal circular holes present to sag).

proposed_rules.description: Cylindrical functional surfaces on FDM-printed shafts suffer layer-stepping (poor roundness/surface finish), degrading press-fit and rotating-fit interfaces.
proposed_rules.look_for: Load-bearing or rotating cylindrical surfaces (shaft journals, bearing seats, gear bores) that will contact a mating part.
proposed_rules.pass_criteria: Cylindrical fit surfaces are called out for post-print machining/reaming, printed on SLA, or the interface tolerance accommodates FDM layer-stepping (approx +/- 0.2-0.3mm).
proposed_rules.fail_criteria: A tight rotating/press fit relies on the as-printed FDM cylindrical surface with no allowance for layer-stepping or roundness error.

proposed_rules.description: FDM shafts loaded in bending/torsion are weakest along the inter-layer bond; print axis relative to load direction is load-bearing for strength.
proposed_rules.look_for: Slender shafts intended to transmit torque or carry transverse load.
proposed_rules.pass_criteria: Print orientation aligns primary stress with in-plane (intra-layer) direction, or the shaft is sized with a safety factor covering ~50% inter-layer strength loss.
proposed_rules.fail_criteria: A torque/bending shaft printed such that the failure plane coincides with a layer boundary, with no strength derating.
